The paradox of analysis (or Langford–Moore paradox ) [ 1 ] is a paradox that concerns how an analysis can be correct or informative but not both. The problem was formulated by philosopher G. E. Moore in his book Principia Ethica , and first named by C. H. Langford in his article "The Notion of Analysis in Moore's Philosophy" (in The Philosophy of G. E. Moore , edited by Paul Arthur Schilpp , Northwestern University, 1942, pp. 319–342).
